steps.do: Create the test file src/toast/ToastTimers.test.tsx that uses vi.useFakeTimers and renders a toast, then unmounts it.
Confirm the file restores real timers in afterEach with vi.useRealTimers.
Confirm the file asserts vi.getTimerCount equals 0 after unmount.
Run only the named timer test and confirm the output shows 1 passed with the timer count at 0.

K-002645.example: Rendering one Toast with a 4000ms duration and unmounting it before 4000ms must leave vi.getTimerCount() at 0. The Vitest run reports 1 passed for that test name.
K-002645.check: The output shows '1 passed' and the timer count assertion holds at 0.
traps: Do not forget vi.useRealTimers() in afterEach, or later tests in the file inherit fake timers.
A timer count of 0 right after render is not proof; the check must happen after unmount.

steps.do: Open src/app.css and add a :root block that sets --nav-bg to #ffffff, --nav-fg to #1a1a1a, and --nav-accent to #0b5cad.
Add a [data-theme='dark'] block that sets --nav-bg to #121212, --nav-fg to #f2f2f2, and --nav-accent to #8ab4f8.
Add color-scheme: light in the :root block and color-scheme: dark in the dark block so scrollbars and form controls follow the theme.
Confirm both theme selectors are present in the file.
Confirm the file is formatted correctly.

K-002646.example: The :root block sets --nav-fg to #1a1a1a and the dark block sets it to #f2f2f2. The nav text uses var(--nav-fg) and never a hex literal.
K-002646.check: grep prints two lines, one for :root and one for [data-theme='dark'], and npx prettier --check src/app.css prints 'All matched files use Prettier code style!'.
traps: Putting hex values directly in Nav.svelte instead of tokens breaks dark mode for every component that copies them. Keep all nav colors as variables in app.css.
Using a .dark class on body when the plan uses data-theme on html creates two sources of truth. Pick one selector and use it everywhere.

steps.do: Create the src/lib directory if it does not exist.
Create src/lib/theme.svelte.js and declare let mode = $state('system') so the module holds a reactive value.
Import browser from $app/environment and read localStorage key 'theme' only when browser is true.
Export a theme object with a getter for mode and a setter that writes the value to localStorage inside a try block.
Type-check the project to confirm the module compiles.

K-002647.example: When localStorage has no 'theme' key, theme.mode is 'system'. Setting theme.mode to 'dark' stores 'dark' under the theme key.
K-002647.check: npx svelte-check --threshold error prints 'svelte-check found 0 errors' and exits 0.
traps: Reading localStorage at module load without checking browser throws during SSR because window is not defined on the server. Guard every browser API with browser.
A plain let instead of $state means components never re-render when the theme changes. Declare the value with $state so it stays reactive.

steps.do: Create the src/lib/components directory if it does not exist.
Create src/lib/components/ThemeToggle.svelte with a button that calls the theme setter on click.
Derive the label with $derived so aria-label reads 'Switch to dark theme' when the resolved theme is light and 'Switch to light theme' when it is dark.
Set min-width and min-height to 44px on the button so the touch target meets the minimum size.
Add a :focus-visible rule with outline 2px solid var(--nav-accent) so keyboard focus is visible in both themes.
Run the toggle test that clicks the button and checks data-theme on the html element.

K-002648.example: When the resolved theme is 'light', clicking the button sets data-theme to 'dark' and changes aria-label to 'Switch to light theme'.
K-002648.check: npx playwright test tests/theme-toggle.spec.ts reports all tests passed with 0 failed and the html data-theme attribute changes after the click.
traps: Using an icon-only button without aria-label leaves screen reader users with no name for the control. Always set aria-label from the derived state.
Removing the focus outline for looks breaks keyboard navigation. Style :focus-visible instead of deleting outlines.

steps.do: Find the %sveltekit.head% placeholder in src/app.html to confirm where the script must go.
Insert an inline script before %sveltekit.head% that reads localStorage key 'theme' inside a try block.
If no stored value exists, fall back to window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches to choose the theme.
Set document.documentElement.dataset.theme to the chosen value inside the script.
Run the no-flash test that loads the page with colorScheme set to dark and checks the attribute before the first paint.

K-002649.example: A visitor with localStorage theme set to 'dark' gets data-theme='dark' on html before the body renders. The page loads without a white flash.
K-002649.check: npx playwright test tests/no-flash.spec.ts reports 1 passed and the assertion that html[data-theme] is set before DOMContentLoaded holds.
traps: Placing the script after %sveltekit.head% lets stylesheets paint first and still produces a flash. Put it before the placeholder.
A theme set in a Svelte $effect runs after hydration, which is too late for first paint. Set the attribute in the inline script instead.

steps.do: Install the axe accessibility engine for Playwright as a dev dependency.
Create tests/nav-contrast.spec.ts that calls page.emulateMedia with colorScheme set to light and again with dark.
In each run, use AxeBuilder with withTags set to wcag2aa and scope the scan to the nav element.
Run the contrast spec for both themes.
If the nav text ratio falls below 4.5:1, change --nav-fg in app.css to a lighter or darker value and rerun the spec.

K-002650.example: The --nav-fg value #6b6b6b on --nav-bg #ffffff measures about 5.3:1 and passes. The value #8a8a8a on white measures about 3.4:1 and fails.
K-002650.check: npx playwright test tests/nav-contrast.spec.ts reports passed for both themes and axe lists 0 color-contrast violations.
traps: Testing only the light theme misses dark theme failures. Run the scan with both color schemes.
A static axe scan does not check hover or focus colors. Add a separate check for those states.

steps.do: Confirm the test runner is installed as a dev dependency.
Confirm the menu component file exists at the expected path.
Run the validation spec with the verbose reporter.
Mount MenuForm with mount from @vue/test-utils, set the input value to an empty string, trigger submit, and assert that the text Required appears in the .error-message element.
Check that the summary line reports zero failed tests.

K-002651.example: The spec sets the name field to an empty string, triggers submit, and expects wrapper.find('.error-message').text() to equal 'Required'. The run must print Tests 4 passed (4) with no failures.
K-002651.check: Vitest prints Test Files 1 passed (1) and Tests 4 passed (4), and the exit code is 0.
traps: Small models often assert before await nextTick, so the error text is not rendered yet.
Always await trigger or nextTick before reading text.
Testing only the valid path skips the error branch, so include at least one invalid case.

steps.do: Start the dev server on port 5173 in a separate terminal and keep it running.
Confirm the menu form binds aria-describedby to each error id.
Confirm aria-invalid is bound to the error state of each field.
Run axe against the demo route that renders the menu form and fail on any violation.
Check that the axe output reports 0 violations for the page.

K-002652.example: When errors.email is set, the input binds aria-invalid to 'true' and aria-describedby to 'email-error', and the span with id email-error reads Enter a valid email. The axe run on /menu-demo must report 0 violations.
K-002652.check: axe prints 0 violations for the page and the command exits with code 0.
traps: Binding aria-describedby to an id that does not exist in the DOM silently breaks the link for screen readers.
Showing the error state only with a red border fails because color alone is not a cue.
Running axe before the dev server responds returns connection errors, not a pass.

steps.do: Find the error text color declared in the menu stylesheet.
Trigger the invalid state on the demo route so the error text is visible before the audit runs.
Run the Lighthouse accessibility audit on the menu demo route and save the JSON report.
Read the color-contrast audit score from the saved report.
Check that the score is 1 and the error text contrast is at least 4.5:1.

K-002653.example: The error text uses #b00020 on #ffffff, a ratio of about 7.0:1, which passes the 4.5:1 minimum for normal text. The jq command must print 1 for the color-contrast score.
K-002653.check: jq prints 1 and the lighthouse-menu.json file exists with the color-contrast audit present.
traps: Large text needs only 3:1, so do not apply that threshold to 14px error messages.
Lighthouse only tests what is rendered, so the invalid state must be shown before the audit.
Hard-coded colors can differ from theme tokens, so check the value in the stylesheet.

steps.do: Confirm Playwright is installed as a dev dependency.
Confirm the menu validation test file exists.
Run the focus and timing spec in Chromium only.
Check that the spec asserts the first invalid field has focus after submit.
Check that the Required message becomes visible within 200ms of submit.

K-002654.example: After clicking submit with an empty name, the spec expects the Name field to have focus and expects the text Required to be visible with a timeout of 200ms. Playwright must report 3 passed with exit code 0.
K-002654.check: Playwright prints 3 passed and the exit code is 0.
traps: The default 5000ms timeout hides slow error rendering, so set the 200ms timeout explicitly.
Focus assertions need the field to exist after submit, so wait for the error before checking focus.
Without the dev server running, the test fails with a navigation timeout, which is not a validation failure.

steps.do: Confirm the Vue ESLint plugin is installed.
Run ESLint on the menu component with zero warnings allowed.
Confirm the submit button and menu options declare min-height of 44px.
Confirm the error text declares a font-size of at least 1rem.
Check that ESLint reports 0 problems and each grep line shows 44px or 1rem.

K-002655.example: The submit button sets min-height: 44px and the error span sets font-size: 1rem, and ESLint with --max-warnings 0 passes on MenuForm.vue. A clean run prints no output and exits with code 0.
K-002655.check: ESLint prints nothing and exits with code 0, and grep prints a min-height line containing 44px.
traps: ESLint passing does not prove the layout is 44px, so check the declared CSS value.
Setting min-height on a wrapper but not the clickable item leaves the real target small.
A value like 2.75rem equals 44px only at a 16px root size, so write the literal value 44px that the check looks for.

steps.do: Confirm vue-tsc is installed as a dev dependency.
Run the Vue type checker over the project without emitting files.
Confirm the defineEmits call declares the validated event with a typed payload.
Confirm defineProps declares the error messages object type.
Check that vue-tsc reports 0 errors.

K-002656.example: The component declares a typed emit for validated with a boolean payload, and the parent listens with @validated on the MenuForm element. vue-tsc --noEmit must exit 0 with no error lines.
K-002656.check: vue-tsc prints no error lines and exits with code 0.
traps: vue-tsc checks types but not runtime validation, so a passing type check does not prove the Required error appears.
Leaving defineEmits untyped lets a wrong payload pass silently.
Plain tsc skips .vue files, so use vue-tsc.

steps.do: Confirm index.html exists in the project root before planning its menu markup.
Count lines in index.html that mention menu, to see how many menu elements the plan must theme.
Name the tokens --menu-bg, --menu-text, --menu-item-hover, and --menu-focus-ring, declared on :root and overridden under [data-theme='dark'].
Set the text target to 4.5:1 contrast and the focus ring and border target to 3:1, per WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11.

K-002657.example: index.html has 1 menu element with the menu word counted 6 times. The plan sets --menu-text to a color with at least 4.5:1 contrast against --menu-bg in both themes.
K-002657.check: The grep -c command prints a number greater than zero, and the plan lists four token names and two numeric contrast targets.
traps: Small models often pick colors by eye and skip the numeric target.
Write 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for focus rings, and keep the same token names in both themes.
Do not put raw colors inside the component selectors.

steps.do: Confirm Node.js is installed and record its version for the test runner.
Check for an existing package.json so the plan uses the project's current test setup.
Confirm Playwright is available through npx so the plan can name a real test runner.
Plan one test per theme using emulated colorScheme values light and dark, and assert the menu background differs between them.
Plan a contrast check that fails if any menu text falls below 4.5:1 in either theme.

K-002658.example: node --version prints v22.11.0 and npx playwright --version prints a version number. The plan adds tests/menu-theme.spec.ts with one test for colorScheme 'light' and one for 'dark'.
K-002658.check: The node and npx commands each print a version number, and the plan names two theme tests and one contrast threshold of 4.5:1.
traps: Small models often plan a visual check with no measurable assertion.
Require a numeric contrast threshold and a computed color difference.
Do not start a dev server or install packages during the plan stage.

steps.do: List every CSS file outside node_modules to find the stylesheets that style the menu.
Search for hardcoded hex colors, which must later be replaced by custom properties.
Search for existing theme hooks such as data-theme, prefers-color-scheme, or color-scheme.
Write each color found, with its role such as text, background, or border, in a plain list. Check each text color against its background and confirm it reaches 4.5:1 contrast.

K-002659.example: The search finds 14 hardcoded hex values in styles/menu.css and no prefers-color-scheme rule. The plan lists each one with its role, for example #1a1a1a as menu item text, and records that it reaches 4.5:1 against the background.
K-002659.check: The rg command prints file path, line number, and matched text for each hit, and the plan maps every hit to a token. The plan states a total count equal to the number of rg lines, and every text color reaches 4.5:1 contrast. Zero data-theme hits means the plan starts from no existing theme.
traps: Small models often guess the colors instead of searching.
Run rg first, because the menu may inherit colors from a global stylesheet.
Do not assume a dark theme exists when the search returns no hits.

steps.do: Search for any existing color-scheme declarations so the plan does not duplicate them.
Count the :root rules in the project so the declaration goes in one place.
Plan one declaration color-scheme: light dark on :root, and a separate color-scheme: dark rule under [data-theme='dark'].
Record that native scrollbars and input controls follow this property, so the menu needs no extra scrollbar styles. Confirm that the menu text still reaches 4.5:1 contrast in both schemes.

K-002660.example: rg finds no color-scheme lines in the project. The plan puts color-scheme: light dark on :root and color-scheme: dark under [data-theme='dark'], and records 4.5:1 contrast for the menu text in both schemes.
K-002660.check: The rg -c command prints a per-file count of :root rules, and the plan names exactly 1 :root rule that sets color-scheme. The menu text in each scheme must reach 4.5:1 contrast.
traps: Small models often add color-scheme to every menu element, which is redundant.
Place it once on :root, because it applies to the whole document.
Do not write color-scheme: dark alone when the page must also support light mode.

steps.do: Count existing localStorage use so the plan reuses any saved preference key.
Count existing matchMedia calls so the plan does not duplicate the system preference check.
Decide that the storage key is menu-theme, with values light and dark, and no stored value means follow the system.
Decide that the switch sets the data-theme attribute on the html element and never changes the stored value on page load. Set the switch control to at least 44px tall.

K-002661.example: rg -c finds no localStorage calls in the project. The plan uses the key menu-theme with values light, dark, or no value, sets document.documentElement.dataset.theme, and sets the switch to 44px tall.
K-002661.check: Both rg -c commands print a per-file count, and zero means no hits. The plan lists exactly 3 states with 1 storage key, and the switch control is at least 44px tall in each state.
traps: Small models often store the system choice as the word system, which breaks the no-value rule.
Store nothing for the system state.
Do not read localStorage before the page renders, because that causes a flash of the wrong theme.

steps.do: Confirm the styles directory exists before searching it for menu sizing.
Search the stylesheets for current min-height and padding values on menu items.
Search for current font-size values on menu items to compare against the 1rem baseline.
Set each menu item to at least 44px height and keep the text at 1rem or larger in every theme.

K-002662.example: The rg search finds padding of 6px on .menu-item in styles/menu.css. The plan raises the item to min-height: 44px and keeps font-size: 1rem.
K-002662.check: The test -d command exits with no output when styles exists, and the rg output lists each current padding or min-height value so the plan can state a 44px target.
traps: Small models often change only colors and leave tiny padding unchanged.
Set min-height: 44px on items and do not rely on line height alone.
Do not shrink text in dark mode to fit more items.

steps.do: Find where ItemList reads the pending flag from the query hook.
Render EmptyState only when the query has resolved and the array length is zero.
Write a Vitest test that mocks a pending query and asserts the empty message is absent.
Run the single test file.

K-002663.example: ItemList.tsx returns <SkeletonRows/> when isPending is true, so the test mocks useItems with {isPending: true, data: undefined} and expects queryByText('No items yet') to be null. The run prints 'Tests 1 passed (1)'.
K-002663.check: Output contains 'Tests 1 passed' and the exit code is 0.
traps: Checking data.length === 0 alone shows the empty state before the fetch starts. Gate on isPending first.
Using getByText instead of queryByText makes the test throw instead of asserting absence.

steps.do: Wrap ItemList in React.Suspense with a fallback of SkeletonRows in ItemsPage.tsx.
Confirm the project type-checks with the fallback typed as ReactNode.
Lint the feature folder with zero warnings allowed.
Run the page test that asserts the fallback rows are in the DOM and EmptyState is not.

K-002664.example: ItemsPage.tsx places <Suspense fallback={<SkeletonRows count={3} />}> around <ItemList/>, and the test expects getAllByRole('row') to have length 3 with no 'No items yet' text. The run prints 'Tests 1 passed (1)'.
K-002664.check: tsc exits 0 with no output, eslint reports 0 problems, and vitest prints 'Tests 1 passed'.
traps: Putting the Suspense boundary inside ItemList lets the empty branch render first. Wrap the component from outside.
A null fallback shows a blank area that users read as an empty result.

steps.do: Start the dev server on port 5173 in its own terminal.
Run Lighthouse on the items route with only the performance category.
Read the cumulative layout shift numeric value from the saved report.

K-002665.example: Lighthouse writes lh-items.json, and jq prints 0.012 after the skeleton swaps to EmptyState. That value is below the 0.1 limit.
K-002665.check: jq prints a number below 0.1, such as 0.012.
traps: Reading the score field gives a 0 to 100 number, not the shift. Use the audit's numericValue.
Running Lighthouse before the dev server is ready records an error page and a meaningless shift.

steps.do: Set the loading label color to #767676 on a #ffffff background in Spinner.module.css.
Confirm the loading element declares aria-live so screen readers announce it.
Run axe against the items route limited to WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 AA rules.

K-002666.example: #767676 on #ffffff gives a contrast ratio of 4.54:1, which passes the 4.5:1 minimum for normal text. The axe run prints '0 violations' and exits 0.
K-002666.check: axe reports 0 violations for color-contrast and exits with code 0.
traps: #888888 on white is about 3.5:1 and fails the 4.5:1 minimum. Pick a darker gray.
Lowering opacity on the label drops its contrast ratio below 4.5:1 even when the base color passes.

steps.do: Search the items feature folder for the empty-state copy string.
Confirm the string appears in EmptyState.tsx only and not in the loading component.
Run the loading test file that checks pending state renders no empty copy.
Run the feature tests with verbose output to confirm both cases ran.

K-002667.example: grep prints one line, src/features/items/EmptyState.tsx:4: No items yet, and vitest reports 'Tests 2 passed (2)' for the pending and resolved-empty cases.
K-002667.check: grep prints exactly one matching line in EmptyState.tsx and vitest prints 'Tests 2 passed (2)'.
traps: Searching the whole repo picks up stories and snapshots and inflates the count. Limit the search to the feature folder.
A passing loading test does not prove the copy is absent from the loader. Confirm the grep result too.

steps.do: Add a Playwright route handler in tests/items-loading.spec.ts that holds the items response for 1500ms. Confirm it is there.
Navigate to the items page with page.goto in the test body. Confirm the call is there.
Put the 200ms timeout on the expect call for the skeleton locator, not on page.goto. Confirm it is there.
Run only the loading spec in Chromium with the line reporter.

K-002668.example: The spec calls expect(page.getByTestId('skeleton-rows')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 200 }) while the route is held 1500ms. Passing output ends with '1 passed'.
K-002668.check: Output ends with '1 passed' and contains no 'Timeout' error.
traps: Putting the 200ms timeout on page.goto checks navigation, not the skeleton. Put it on the expect.
If the held response is shorter than the timeout, the test passes without proving the skeleton appeared first.

steps.do: Search for existing ProgressView spinners so the plan can replace them where needed.
Plan a static sample value named Item.placeholder to fill the rows while loading.
Plan the list to show exactly 5 placeholder rows with the .redacted(reason: .placeholder) modifier.
Count existing uses of redacted so the plan records the current starting point.

K-002669.example: The plan shows 5 rows of Item.placeholder with .redacted(reason: .placeholder) while state is loading. rg -c 'redacted' Sources returns 0 before the build stage.
K-002669.check: The plan names the row count of 5 and the modifier .redacted(reason: .placeholder), and the rg count matches the starting point.
traps: Small models add a fixed sleep to simulate loading, which hides real timing. Use the real load state to drive the placeholder. Do not use redacted on views that show live data the layout cannot predi…

steps.do: Create the plan folder for timing budgets.
Create the budget file that will hold the timing limit.
Write the budget line into the file: a cached tab shows its first content within 200ms of being tapped.
Plan that the spinner appears only after 500ms, and the placeholder rows appear immediately.
Search the tab code for fixed sleeps, because the budget forbids them.

K-002670.example: The budget says a cached tab shows content within 200ms, and the spinner waits 500ms. rg -n 'sleep' Sources returns no matches in the tab code.
K-002670.check: rg -n 'sleep' Sources prints nothing, and rg -c '200ms' docs/plans/tab-budget.md prints 1.
traps: Small models add Task.sleep to fake a delay, which breaks the budget. A plan line with a time limit is not a measurement, so the build stage must add an XCTest or XCTMetric check. Do not write a time…

steps.do: Start a static server for the project root on port 8080 in its own terminal.
Install the Playwright test runner as a dev dependency.
Download the Chromium build that Playwright drives.
Run the nav validation spec against the local server.
Confirm the spec counts the two required nav fields as invalid.

K-002671.example: The nav form at http://localhost:8080/nav.html has a required search input with pattern='[a-z0-9 ]{2,40}' and a required email input. The spec clicks submit on the empty form and expects exactly 2 elements matching :invalid inside the form.
K-002671.check: Playwright prints '2 passed' with no failures, and the grep prints 1.
traps: A form with novalidate skips native checks, so the spec can pass without testing the browser's validation at all.
If the server is not running, Playwright fails with net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED, which looks like a validation failure but is not one.
Checking only :invalid shows errors before the user has typed anything, so check :user-invalid for the after-interaction state.

steps.do: Install html-validate as a dev dependency.
Validate the nav markup file.
Count the lines that contain the required attribute.
Count label elements that carry a for attribute.
Confirm no field ships with aria-invalid hard-coded to true.

K-002672.example: nav.html has a search input with id='q' and a matching label for='q', plus an email input with id='email' and its own label. html-validate should report zero errors, and the required and label counts should both be 2.
K-002672.check: html-validate prints no errors and exits 0, the aria-invalid grep prints 0, and the required and label counts each equal the number of inputs.
traps: A label for value that matches no input id fails html-validate but looks correct on screen.
Hard-coding aria-invalid=true on page load makes screen readers announce errors before the user has typed anything.
The required grep also matches comments, so read the matched lines before trusting the count.

steps.do: Install the axe command line runner as a dev dependency.
Load the nav page with errors shown and run axe against the WCAG AA tags.
Confirm the error text color is set in the nav stylesheet.
Confirm each invalid field points to its error message with aria-describedby.

K-002673.example: nav-error.html shows error text in #b00020 on a #ffffff background, which is well above the 4.5:1 minimum for normal text. The page has 2 invalid fields, so the grep should return 2 aria-describedby attributes.
K-002673.check: axe reports 0 violations, and the aria-describedby grep prints 2, matching the number of invalid fields.
traps: Running axe on the empty page before submit skips the error state, so the result says nothing about the errors.
Red error text on a red field background can fall below 4.5:1 even when the text color alone passes.
The axe CLI needs the local server running first, or it reports a failed page load instead of a pass.

steps.do: Install Lighthouse as a dev dependency.
Run only the accessibility category against the nav error page.
Read the accessibility score from the JSON report.
Confirm the label audit passed for the form fields.

K-002674.example: The Lighthouse run on nav-error.html reports an accessibility score of 0.96 and a label audit score of 1. Both values come from the same lh-nav.json file.
K-002674.check: The first jq prints a value of 0.9 or higher, and the second jq prints 1.
traps: A perfect Lighthouse score does not prove that the form can be completed with a keyboard.
Lighthouse needs a local Chrome or Chromium install, and without one it fails before writing any report.
The score is a weighted mix of audits, so a passing score can hide one failed label check.

steps.do: Confirm the nav stylesheet sets a minimum height of 44px on form buttons.
Run the target size spec at a 375px wide viewport.
List the lines in the spec that read the bounding box.

K-002675.example: At a 375px viewport, the submit button measures 46px tall in the test output. The spec asserts that box.height is at least 44 and box.width is at least 44.
K-002675.check: The grep for min-height prints 1 or more, Playwright prints '1 passed', and the boundingBox grep shows the line where the height assertion is made.
traps: An inline element ignores min-height, so the measured height stays at the line height and the test fails.
The 44px check uses CSS pixels, so changing the device pixel ratio does not change the result.
Padding without box-sizing border-box can change the measured box size, so the test may pass or fail for the wrong reason.

steps.do: Install the Playwright test runner if the project does not already have it.
Run the timing spec that submits an invalid nav form.
Confirm the spec asserts the 200ms budget.
Confirm the error element uses role alert so screen readers announce it.

K-002676.example: After clicking submit on an empty nav form, the element .nav-error becomes visible in 84ms as measured with performance.now(). The spec asserts that the measured time is less than 200.
K-002676.check: Playwright prints '1 passed', the first grep prints 1, and the second grep prints 1.
traps: Measuring from page load instead of from the submit click hides slow error rendering.
A timer that is too short can flake under load, so run the spec several times before trusting a single pass.
Adding role=alert to every error makes screen readers announce them all at once, so use it only on the summary message.

steps.do: Open forms/signup.html and find every img element inside the form.
Add width and height attributes to each img that match the icon's intrinsic pixel size, such as width='16' and height='16'.
Count the img tags in the form file; this should match the number of icons.
Count the lines that contain a width attribute; this should equal the img count.
Run Lighthouse on the form page and read the cumulative layout shift audit.

K-002677.example: The lock icon at img src='icons/lock.svg' on line 12 gets width='16' and height='16', and the file has 3 icon imgs. grep -c returns 3 for both patterns and Lighthouse reports a CLS score of 1.
K-002677.check: Both grep counts print 3 and the Lighthouse cumulative-layout-shift audit has score 1 with no flagged elements.
traps: Small models set the size only in CSS, which does not reserve space before the stylesheet loads. Use the HTML attributes.
Do not guess the intrinsic size; read it from the SVG or image file first.

steps.do: Find every script tag on the form page to see where each one loads.
Add the defer attribute to the validate.js script tag, or move the tag to just before the closing body tag.
Count the script tags that have a src attribute; the validation script should be one of them.
